chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūrī, Abū Sa‘īd, who said:

‘Abdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Manī‘ ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus ibn Ya‘qūb ibn ‘Ammār, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever misses ‘Arafah in ‘Arafāt but catches it by the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), has not missed it. And verily, Allāh, the Blessed and Exalted, begins with the people of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) before the people of ‘Arafāt. Then he said: He mixes them with Himself [in Himself].

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: The plain of Arafat, the central station of the Hajj pilgrimage
key_terms.عَرَفَةُ: The Day of Arafah, the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, a pivotal day in Hajj
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.يُبْدَأُ: He begins (referring to God's bestowal of favor or attention)
key_terms.يُخَالِطُهُمْ: He mixes them (referring to divine proximity or union)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the spiritual equivalence of visiting Imam al-Ḥusayn’s (a.s.) grave on the Day of ‘Arafah with the pilgrimage itself, a concept rooted in the Shia belief that his grave serves as a terrestrial counterpart to the celestial ‘Arafah. The narration highlights a unique divine priority, where God begins bestowing favor upon those at his shrine before those at the actual plain of ‘Arafah, underscoring the Imam’s role as the ultimate intercessor and locus of divine proximity.
